requirements.requirement: Keep the installed curl package at its current version when system updates are performed on node1.
requirements.summary: The initial package was curl-7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64. A persistent yum exclusion for curl was added and confirmed through yum's parsed configuration; the same package version, working executable, effective exclusion, and clean RPM verification remained after reboot. The attempted update could not reach a transaction because no repositories were enabled, so update behavior was established through the effective configuration rather than a successful repository-backed update.

overall_summary: The task outcome is satisfied: node1 retains curl-7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64 under a persistent, effectively parsed yum exclusion. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: pre-restart identity and curl health were captured, restart was acknowledged, the post-restart boot identity changed, and curl configuration and integrity recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the reboot.
limitations: No enabled repositories were available, so the captured yum update attempt ended before an actual update transaction; there is no direct repository-backed demonstration that another package updates while curl remains held.
The lifecycle package-health probe timed out both before and after execution, although targeted `rpm -V curl` verification succeeded after reboot.

Restart evidence directly covers the relevant curl package/configuration and general node recovery; there was no separate application data or cluster state applicable to this single-node package-hold task.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were observed. Editing /etc/yum.conf was the required implementation change, the update attempt was bounded verification, and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. The two package-install attempts failed before evidence of any package-state change. No failed services, new exposures, or executor residue were observed after completion; socket and temporary-file differences were normal reboot-related identity/PID changes.
